thread.title: Apple Pay surpassed 1.8 billion transactions in Apple's fiscal Q1 2019 (AAPL, TGT, JACK)

author: Rachel Green
title: Apple Pay surpassed 1.8 billion transactions in Apple's fiscal Q1 2019 (AAPL, TGT, JACK)
text:
This story was delivered to Business Insider Intelligence " Payments Briefing " subscribers hours before appearing on Business Insider. To be the first to know, please click here .
Apple Pay reached over 1.8 billion transactions in Apple's fiscal Q1 2019 (ended December 29, 2018), which is more than twice the volume the mobile wallet saw during its fiscal Q1 2018.
Justin Sullivan/Getty Images
In the company's earnings call , Apple CEO Tim Cook highlighted a few factors that drove transaction volume growth.
Apple Pay is now live in 27 markets globally. Apple Pay has been pursuing wider global acceptance, launching in Germany, Belgium, and Kazakhstan in December 2018. Cook noted that Germany's receptiveness to Apple Pay upon launch was successful, "...with Duetsche Bank reporting more activations for Apple Pay in one week than for Android in an entire year." Global expansion is integral to Apple Pay's growth given the slow uptake of mobile wallets in the US: A recent study suggests that only 14% of US consumers use mobile wallets. An estimated 85% of Apple Pay users come from outside the US, likely because many non-US markets are already attuned to contactless payments, which can precipitate demand for mobile wallets. And it's been building out its domestic merchant acceptance network as well.Cook noted that "merchant adoption reached new milestones," pointing to the addition of 3,000 Speedway locations and mentioning the upcoming rollout to Target, Taco Bell, and Jack-in-the-Box retail locations, all of which will expand the mobile wallet's acceptance network significantly. Developing a universal acceptance network in the US can aid in driving Apple Pay adoption by making it easier for consumers to form habits if they can use the mobile wallet regularly. Emphasizing US growth is imperative, given that the US is the largest iPhone market globally and has the potential for widespread adoption.
